about: The labs, in the recommended order. Each lab is one subject: Learn (short pages in our own words, each with passages from Microsoft Learn through the concepts it names, and a quiz), Do (tasks in the simulated environment, checked by code; {placeholders} are filled from the environment, src/labs/labs.ts), and Challenge (ready-made exercises, ids from content/scenarios/ready-made.json). A planned lab is listed so learners see the whole path.

labs.title: How a call finds its way
labs.summary: What Contact Center does, and the path a call takes from phone number to representative.

learn.title: What Contact Center does
text: Dynamics 365 Contact Center lets a company answer its customers on channels like chat, messaging and voice. This training is about voice: customers phone a number, and a representative helps them.

Between the ringing phone and the representative, unified routing decides where the call goes and who takes it. It first adds information to the call, then sends it to a queue and assigns it to a person who is free.

learn.title: The path of a call
text: Every call follows the same path. The phone number belongs to a voice channel. The voice channel belongs to a workstream: the workstream takes the call in and decides where it goes.
Many workstreams have an AI agent that answers first, like an IVR menu. Then the workstream's route-to-queue rules pick a queue, and the queue's assignment method picks a representative.

learn.title: The caller's answer
text: When an AI agent asks “What is your call about?”, the caller's answer is kept on the call in a context variable, for example SelectedMenuItem = Billing.
Routing rules can read that value. That's how a choice in the menu leads to a queue.

learn.title: Queues and the safety net
text: A queue holds calls until a representative takes them. Only the members of a queue get its calls.
A call that no route-to-queue rule picks up isn't lost: it goes to the workstream's fallback queue. That keeps the call, but the people there may not be the right ones.

learn.title: Where you work in this training
text: Admin center: a simulation of the Copilot Service admin center, where you set things up. It has Microsoft's menu and field names, with our own look.
Diagram: how everything connects, from phone numbers to people. Phone: call any number and follow the call step by step. Agent: be a representative or a supervisor in the workspace.
Nothing here is real: the environment, the people and the phone numbers are made up, so you can change anything.

quiz.question: What decides which queue a call goes to?
options: The phone number on its own
The language of the voice channel
quiz.why: The workstream's route-to-queue rules pick the queue. The phone number only decides which workstream takes the call.

quiz.question: A call matches none of the route-to-queue rules. Where does it go?
options: To the first queue in the list
quiz.why: The fallback queue is the safety net for calls no rule picks up.

quiz.question: Where does the caller's answer to the IVR end up?
options: In a context variable on the call
In the name of the queue
quiz.why: The AI agent stores the answer in a context variable, and routing rules can check it.

labs.title: Phone numbers and the voice channel
labs.summary: Where calls come in: numbers, voice channels, and which workstream answers.

labs.title: Workstreams
labs.summary: What a workstream does with a call: its fallback queue and how it distributes work.

labs.title: Queues and representatives
labs.summary: Queues, who is in them, and what a representative needs to get a call: presence and capacity.

learn.title: Queues
text: A queue holds calls until a representative takes them. Each queue is for one kind of work; calls need a voice queue.
You create queues in the admin center under Queues, then Advanced queues.

learn.title: Who is in a queue
text: Representatives are the people who take calls. You add them to a queue as its users.
Only members of a queue get its calls. A queue without members holds calls that nobody can answer.

learn.title: Presence
text: Presence says whether a representative can take work right now: Available, Busy, Away, Do not disturb or Offline (in this training Do not disturb is called Busy - DND). A representative sets it at the top of the workspace.

Each workstream lists the presences it assigns work to. In this training's workstreams that's Available and Busy. In the product, presence also changes by itself as a representative's capacity fills up; the training doesn't do that.

learn.title: Capacity
text: A capacity profile says how much work a representative can take at the same time, for example one call.
After a call ends, the representative is in wrap-up. Their capacity stays in use until they close the session, so they don't get a new call in the middle of their notes.

learn.title: Who gets the call
text: When a call waits in a queue, the queue's assignment method picks one of the members who can take it: in an allowed presence, with capacity left.
Least active is the default for voice queues: the call goes to the member who has been least active.

quiz.question: Mia is Available, but she isn't a member of the Billing queue. Can routing give her a Billing call?
options: No: only members of a queue get its calls
Only if she has the right skill
quiz.why: Assignment only looks at the queue's own members.

quiz.question: Which representatives can get calls from this training's voice workstreams?
options: Those who are Available or Busy, with capacity left
Anyone who is signed in, whatever their presence
quiz.why: The workstream's allowed presences are Available and Busy, and the representative needs capacity left.

quiz.question: A representative selected End. When is their capacity free for the next call?
options: When they close the session after wrap-up
quiz.why: In wrap-up the capacity stays in use until the session is closed.

labs.title: Assignment and capacity
labs.summary: How a queue picks a representative: assignment methods and capacity profiles.

labs.title: The IVR and context variables
labs.summary: What the AI agent asks, and how the answer becomes something routing can use.

labs.title: Route-to-queue rules
labs.summary: Rules that send a call to a queue: conditions, order, hit policy and the fallback queue.

learn.title: From an answer to a queue
text: The IVR keeps the caller's answer in a context variable. The workstream's route-to-queue ruleset holds rules that read it.
Each rule says: if this is true about the call, send it to that queue.

learn.title: Writing a rule
text: Open the workstream, then its ruleset under Route to queues, and select Create rule. Give the rule a name, add a condition, and pick the queue.
A condition compares a field with a value, for example SelectedMenuItem Equals Billing. The value must be exactly what the IVR sends; “Billing invoice” doesn't match “Billing”.

learn.title: When more than one rule matches
text: The rules are a decision list, in order. When several rules match and no queue is overflowing, the first rule in the list wins.
The rule hit policy says what happens when a queue is overflowing: Hit-all moves on to the next matching rule; Hit-first stays with the first one.

learn.title: When no rule matches
text: A call that no rule picks up goes to the workstream's fallback queue. A new menu choice without a rule always ends there.
So when calls pile up in the fallback queue, look for a choice that has no rule, or a rule whose value doesn't match.

learn.title: Sharing calls between queues
text: One rule can share its calls between up to five queues, with a percentage for each that adds up to 100, for example 70% to one team and 30% to another.

quiz.question: The IVR sends “Billing”. Your rule checks SelectedMenuItem Equals “Billing invoice”. What happens to the call?
options: The rule doesn't match, so another rule or the fallback queue takes the call
quiz.why: The value has to match what the IVR sends.

quiz.question: Two rules match a call, and neither queue is overflowing. Which queue does the call go to?
options: The queue of the first rule in the decision list
The queue of the last rule
The queue with the most members
quiz.why: Learn: the system selects the queue of the first rule in the list.

quiz.question: Where do you add a route-to-queue rule?
options: On the workstream, in its route-to-queue ruleset
quiz.why: Routing rules belong to the workstream.
